name: DJ Spanish Fly
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 memphis-rap — DJ Spanish Fly
The Quietus — DJ Spanish Fly interview — http://thequietus.com/articles/05588-dj-spanish-fly-interview
Future Audio Workshop — Memphis hip hop I — https://futureaudioworkshop.com/memphis-hip-hop-i/
notes: "The Godfather of Memphis Rap", and the slowest band in the whole section — his own figure is "60bpm or even less" with the backbeat on 3, which is 108–124 straight. The parameter that makes this model his rather than the lane's is that **the bass line is the written part**: he played it by hand on a Juno-6, so `bassline.rhythm` is `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.55 across a 22-semitone register — the most melodic low end in this batch — while the chords are a single-chord drone carried by `impliedByRiff`, `chordDurationBeats` 8–32 and a vamp-weighted `harmonicRhythm` rather than by progressions. Everything above it is thin by design: the mature kit is TR-808 kick plus cowbell as essentially the entire pattern (`percs.densityPerBar` 6–10 at 0 dB, kick 2–3 a bar), snares sharp and digital, hats minimal (velocities 0.4–0.62 under a plain 8th base). The cassette-to-cassette chain is authored as the loosest timing in this batch — `quantizeStrength` 0.66, `velocityVar` 0.32 — and the arrangement is loop-and-extend: 24–32 bar verses and a structure long enough to run "seven or eight minutes", with `switchUpProb` at 0.01. ⚠ `medium`, per the research's high-medium: the tempo, the equipment, the sample sources and the technique are all in his own words, **and the pre-1990 origin is deliberately outside the modeled era** rather than estimated. ⚠ `timbreHint` is `spacey_keys` for the Juno; his melodic layer is a found loop rather than a written part, so treat the lead as the raw sample it stands in for. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [51, 79] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 36 against a bass reaching 50, an overlap of 15. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 745 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 937/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 937/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.34 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 937/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
